well...depending on what your use your computer for, you are possibly fine to keep your current rig and just install linux on it. All kinds of flavors. If you like to geek out, try a hobbyist build like crunchbang or archlinux (arch has a pretty impressive wiki... not too much hand holding, but "the info is there if you just look"). Those flavors tend to be "barebones", that is, super lightweight with not too much support software without you personally installing it. If you're looking for more of a user friendly build, Ubuntu has always "just worked" for me. I am personally not too happy with it though, as it is significantly bloated with additional software that you'll probably never use. Additionally, Ubuntu has gotten into bed with Microsoft so time will tell the ramifications of that. I heard a lot of good things about linux mint, which is also rather user friendly, but they were recently subject to a pretty nefarious hack (supposedly resolved) so use at your own risk.

Using linux on a day to day basis is work. There's no other way to say it. If you used OSX before and are semi-familiar with the unix shell, you'll probably have little troubles. If you haven't, don't let it discourage you. If you like nerdy things it's fun to learn. IRC and google searches will solve almost every problem you could come across
